title: Quick Integration Studio: scripts and heuristics (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope
This is a working playbook for the "Quick Integration Studio" — a local-first devloop environment + small test harness for customers to validate SDK integration and common failure modes in 20–30 minutes. Focus: reproducible onboarding scripts, lightweight telemetry probes, deterministic smoke tests, and explicit recovery paths.

Audience
- Engineers evaluating Redwood SDKs (JS, Python, Go)
- Developer advocates running live demos
- Solutions/SEs prepping customer sandbox guides

Goals (non-governance)
- Give a 3-step path: install -> run sample -> sanity+failure test.
- Provide small, copy-paste scripts that work offline with a local stub and online against Redwood hosted API.
- Surface minimal telemetry items to decide "safe to prod" (latency, error class, token cost estimate).

Quick 3-step flow (30 minutes)
1) Bootstrap (3–5 min)
  - git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-studio-prototypes
  - cd sdk-studio-prototypes/studio-sample
  - ./scripts/bootstrap.sh  # installs node, python venv, tiny stub server
2) Run canonical sample (10–12 min)
  - Start local stub: ./scripts/run-stub.sh
  - In other shell: ./scripts/run-sample-js.sh OR ./scripts/run-sample-py.sh
  - Expected: streaming chat lines printed, 0 E2E errors, stub responds within 20ms
3) Sanity + failure tests (10–12 min)
  - Token cost smoke: ./scripts/estimate-cost.sh sample-prompt.txt
  - Latency under load: ./scripts/load-smoke.sh --concurrency 8 --requests 50
  - Failure injection: ./scripts/inject-502.sh then re-run sample to validate retry/backoff is triggered

Studio heuristics and guardrails (why these checks)
- Local stub must replicate three behaviors: streaming chunks, KV cache TTL semantics, and 429/502 error shapes. These are the most common integration surprises.
- Telemetry must include (1) request-id, (2) model-version, (3) token-count-estimate, (4) latency P50/P95, (5) error-class. Minimal but actionable.
- For streaming demos, prefer line-delimited JSON events to avoid partial render confusion.

Scripts: patterns and examples (copy-paste friendly)
- run-sample-py.sh (excerpt)
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  source venv/bin/activate
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=test_local_key
  python samples/quick_chat.py --url http://localhost:8080 --stream true

- estimate-cost.sh (pseudo)
  # token estimate: tokens = approx(len(prompt)/4) + len(completion)/4
  # call local estimator to print $0.0004/token for curated model

Failure and recovery scenarios (explicit playbook)
1) 502 from upstream during streaming
  - Detect: connection closed + last-chunk incomplete
  - Recovery: client should display partial output + run a background retry for missing suffix using model-variant-fallback (lower-cost quantized variant)
2) 429 / rate-limited on bursts
  - Detect: 429 with Retry-After header or 429 + no header
  - Recovery: linear backoff then fail fast to degraded route (smaller model or cached prefix response). Document a sample circuit-breaker config for SDK (example in scripts/circuit-breaker.json).
3) Increased token inflation after prompt template change
  - Detect: sudden token-count jump > 2x baseline across rolling 100 reqs
  - Recovery: alert dev, gate rollout, run differential evals against golden prompt set

Telemetry probe examples (what to capture)
- client.request_id (string)
- model.name, model.version (string)
- route.used (hosted|dedicated|private)
- tokens.input, tokens.output (integers as strings in this doc)
- latency.ms_p50, ms_p95
- error.code (e.g., 502, 429, TIMEOUT)
- fallback.used (true|false)

Checklist for demo readiness (quick)
- [ ] sample runs end-to-end (local stub) in < 30s
- [ ] streaming renders are line-buffered and flush correctly
- [ ] retries and circuit-breaker exercised manually
- [ ] token estimates within 15% of hosted response cost
- [ ] telemetry events appear in local aggregator and surface request-id

Integration notes for SEs (short tips)
- If customer is on Private, switch sample config to use VPC-hosted endpoint and ensure SDK can accept self-signed CA (scripts/config-private.yaml included).
- For Dedicated customers, add an autoscaling smoke: ./scripts/dedicated-load-check.sh which hits the dedicated pool tag; ensures warmup latency < baseline.

Open TODOs / research bits
- Add a one-click GH Codespace devcontainer that preps the studio environment (easier for field demos).
- Automate golden prompt regression runner and wire to Optimize as a quality gate.
- Add small web UI wrapper for streaming playback to demonstrate partial outputs and recovery UX.

Notes to self (scratchpad)
- Keep scripts intentionally minimal so SEs can copy them into customer repos.
- Avoid hardcoding API keys; use sample env var patterns and a credentials quickswap helper.

Attachments and reference files in this folder
- scripts/ (bootstrap + stub + samples)
- samples/ (py/js quick_chat, prompts)
- scripts/circuit-breaker.json (sample rule config)
- docs/studio-runbook-short.md (small runbook we can expand)

If you run the studio and hit a weird edge, ping #devexp-studio and drop the local stub logs (scripts/logs/latest.log).

---
Author: Aisha Patel (draft)
Feedback welcome — especially on: which failure modes are most useful to customers, and which telemetry fields feel like "noise" vs. "actionable".
